title_or_table: Medicaid and CHIP Updated Renewal Outcomes, national rows (state code US)
table_id: data.medicaid.gov dataset e6205a51-e6d7-4849-9882-4483b8a28c41, October 2024 release, metrics 5 to 5d
observation_period: Renewals due March 2023 to March 2024, by reporting month
geography: United States, the sum of the states’ reports (checked equal by script)
universe_or_base: Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries due for renewal in each month, as states reported them to CMS
vintage: Updated renewal outcomes, October 2024 final release (dataset modified November 1, 2024)
qualification: State-reported counts, "updated" to show renewals that were pending three months after they were due; states began the unwinding in different months (4 reported renewals due in March 2023, and all 50 states and DC from July 2023), and the file ends with renewals due in March 2024, before the unwinding ended in every state. A person due in two months of the file counts twice.

month.description: reporting month: the month the renewals were due

states_reporting.description: states and DC with a renewal count that month (51 possible)

renewed_ex_parte.description: renewed on an ex parte basis, from information the state already held (metric 5a1)

renewed_form.description: renewed on the return of a renewal form (metric 5a2)

ended_ineligible.description: determined ineligible on the return of a renewal form (metric 5b)

ended_procedural.description: terminated for a procedural or administrative reason (metric 5c)

pending.description: renewal still pending at the end of the update window (metric 5d, updated)

unaccounted.description: due less renewed, ended and pending, computed by the studio; 0 when the row adds up

notes: Procedural reason, in CMS’s words (read November 13, 2026): its file names metric 5c “Total beneficiaries whose coverage was terminated for a procedural or administrative reason”, beside metric 5b, “Total beneficiaries determined ineligible for Medicaid and CHIP based on the return of a renewal form”. The description of CMS’s original renewal data (Medicaid and CHIP CAA Reporting Metrics, data.medicaid.gov) adds: “States that held procedural terminations reflect these data in metric 5d as pending renewals along with renewals that were due but not completed by the end of the reporting period.” The file, its data dictionary and both datasets’ descriptions give no examples of a procedural reason; CMS’s Data Sources and Metrics Definitions Overview, on medicaid.gov, refused this container (HTTP 403) and was not read.

What a procedural ending is, in the rules’ words (BC-S9, read November 13, 2026). The renewal rule in force through the file’s period, 42 CFR 435.916(a)(3)(iii) (77 FR 17210, March 23, 2012; eCFR as of October 1, 2023), tells the state to “Reconsider in a timely manner the eligibility of an individual who is terminated for failure to submit the renewal form or necessary information, if the individual subsequently submits the renewal form within 90 days after the date of termination”. CMS’s 2024 eligibility rule (89 FR 22780, April 2, 2024) speaks of “individuals who are terminated for procedural reasons (that is, because they did not respond to the State’s request for additional information)” (at 22800) and of “losing coverage due to procedural reasons, including, for example, failure to return paperwork” (at 22781). Section 1902(tt)(1) of the Social Security Act, under which states reported these counts, names the two kinds apart: those terminated and, of them, those terminated “for procedural reasons”. No record read says how many people ended for a procedural reason were still eligible, or which reason was most common.
